title: Titanium Dental Abutment
alloyReason: ASTM F136 Ti-6Al-4V ELI is specified for this dental implant-grade component where controlled interstitials deliver high fatigue strength (>600 MPa @10^7 cyc) and corrosion resistance for permanent implantable devices. This rationale is driven by modular dental abutment retaining screw and fat life requirements.
process: CNC swiss turning for dental geometry
Ultrasonic clean Class 10k for net-shape tolerance
surfaceTreatment: Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for modular dental abutment application
commonFailures: Fatigue fracture at thread root under cyclic bending - resolved by thread rolling (not cutting) for compressive stress — critical for modular dental abutment performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Dental Abutment suitable for Modular dental abutment retaining screw?
faq.a: Titanium Dental Abutment uses Ti-6Al-4V ELI because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address dental operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Dental Abutment?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Dental Abutment is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for modular dental abutment requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Dental Abutment require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. modular dental abutment components require Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for modular dental abutment application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Dental Abutment shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Dental Abutment includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet modular dental abutment specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Abutment screw / Dental abutment dental components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
